x-fal-metadata.about:
Gemini 3 Pro Image is a text-to-image model that generates images from text descriptions.

Decompression-bomb inputs to ``image_urls`` are rejected upstream by
``validate_image_async`` (called from ``GoogleAIClient._format_image``):
the validator now enforces a header-only ``max_image_pixels`` cap
(default 89,478,485 ≈ PIL's ``MAX_IMAGE_PIXELS``) *before* any pixel
decode, so oversized inputs raise a deterministic 422
``image_too_large`` instead of OOM-killing the runner and taking out
every multiplexed request on it (``max_multiplexing=20``).

model.description:
Model to use for background removal.
            The 'General Use (Light)' model is the original model used in the BiRefNet repository.
            The 'General Use (Light 2K)' model is the original model used in the BiRefNet repository but trained with 2K images.
            The 'General Use (Heavy)' model is a slower but more accurate model.
            The 'Matting' model is a model trained specifically for matting images.
            The 'Portrait' model is a model trained specifically for portrait images.
            The 'General Use (Dynamic)' model supports dynamic resolutions from 256x256 to 2304x2304.
            The 'General Use (Light)' model is recommended for most use cases.

            The corresponding models are as follows:
            - 'General Use (Light)': BiRefNet
            - 'General Use (Light 2K)': BiRefNet_lite-2K
            - 'General Use (Heavy)': BiRefNet_lite
            - 'Matting': BiRefNet-matting

x-fal-metadata.about:
Gemini 3 Pro Image is a text-to-image model that generates images from text descriptions.

Decompression-bomb inputs to ``image_urls`` are rejected upstream by
``validate_image_async`` (called from ``GoogleAIClient._format_image``):
the validator now enforces a header-only ``max_image_pixels`` cap
(default 89,478,485 ≈ PIL's ``MAX_IMAGE_PIXELS``) *before* any pixel
decode, so oversized inputs raise a deterministic 422
``image_too_large`` instead of OOM-killing the runner and taking out
every multiplexed request on it (``max_multiplexing=20``).

cns_power_gamma.title: CNS Power Gamma
cns_power_gamma.description: Exponent on the residual (1 - gamma). Higher concentrates noise more aggressively on unresolved bands; lower is gentler and flatter. No effect under 'approximation', where gamma is uniform.

cns_gamma_divider.title: CNS Gamma Divider
cns_gamma_divider.description: Divides gamma first, weakening the coloring (pushing it toward uniform white noise). Paper uses 1.73 for distilled/unguided and 25.0 for CFG/base, so raise this for the /base (CFG) endpoints.

cns_s_churn.title: CNS Noise Strength
cns_s_churn.description: How much stochastic (colored) noise is injected after each step. 0 = CNS off, i.e. pure deterministic flow-matching (identical to normal klein); higher = more stochasticity. Turn this first; the other CNS parameters only matter when s_churn > 0.

cns_alpha_tilt_end.title: CNS Alpha Tilt End
cns_alpha_tilt_end.description: Frequency tilt at the end of sampling. Positive boosts high frequencies (fine texture/detail); negative boosts low frequencies (structure). The default favors low-frequency structure at the end.

enable_cns.title: Enable CNS
enable_cns.description: Enable Colored Noise Sampling (CNS), a stochastic SDE sampler. Off by default; when enabled the cns_* parameters below take effect.

cns_gamma_source.title: CNS Gamma Source
cns_gamma_source.description: Where the per-frequency progress signal gamma(f, t) comes from. 'approximation' is self-contained but uniform across bands, so the frequency shaping comes entirely from the alpha-tilt parameters. 'matrix' uses the precomputed per-band gamma for true spectral-bias-aware coloring (more noise to genuinely under-resolved bands).

cns_alpha_use_fnorm.title: CNS Frequency-Weighted Tilt
cns_alpha_use_fnorm.description: Use a smooth, frequency-position-weighted tilt (exp(alpha * f)) instead of a flat (1 + alpha) multiplier.

cns_alpha_exp_sharpness.title: CNS Exponential Tilt Sharpness
cns_alpha_exp_sharpness.description: How sharp the exponential tilt-interpolation curve is. Only used when exponential interpolation is enabled.

cns_energy_scale.title: CNS Energy Scale
cns_energy_scale.description: Global multiplier on the injected colored noise after variance normalisation. <1 slightly damps the kick, >1 amplifies it (paper: 0.98 unguided, 0.998 guided).

cns_alpha_exp_interp.title: CNS Exponential Tilt Interpolation
cns_alpha_exp_interp.description: Use an exponential (vs linear) curve for the start-to-end tilt transition across sampling steps.

cns_num_freq_bins.title: CNS Frequency Bins
cns_num_freq_bins.description: How many radial frequency bands the spectrum is split into. More bands = finer-grained coloring.

cns_alpha_tilt_start.title: CNS Alpha Tilt Start
cns_alpha_tilt_start.description: Frequency tilt at the start of sampling, interpolated toward the end value over steps. Positive boosts high frequencies (fine texture/detail); negative boosts low frequencies (structure).

cns_power_gamma.title: CNS Power Gamma
cns_power_gamma.description: Exponent on the residual (1 - gamma). Higher concentrates noise more aggressively on unresolved bands; lower is gentler and flatter. No effect under 'approximation', where gamma is uniform.

cns_gamma_divider.title: CNS Gamma Divider
cns_gamma_divider.description: Divides gamma first, weakening the coloring (pushing it toward uniform white noise). Paper uses 1.73 for distilled/unguided and 25.0 for CFG/base, so raise this for the /base (CFG) endpoints.

cns_s_churn.title: CNS Noise Strength
cns_s_churn.description: How much stochastic (colored) noise is injected after each step. 0 = CNS off, i.e. pure deterministic flow-matching (identical to normal klein); higher = more stochasticity. Turn this first; the other CNS parameters only matter when s_churn > 0.

cns_alpha_tilt_end.description: Frequency tilt at the end of sampling. Positive boosts high frequencies (fine texture/detail); negative boosts low frequencies (structure). The default favors low-frequency structure at the end.

x-fal-metadata.about:
Edit or generate images using 1-3 reference images.

Wan 2.6 Image Edit features:
- Style transfer from reference images
- Subject consistency across generated images
- Multi-image input for complex compositions (1-3 images)
- Generate 1-4 output images
- Prompt expansion with LLM optimization

Image requirements:
- Formats: JPEG, JPG, PNG (no alpha), BMP, WEBP
- Resolution: 384-5000 pixels (width and height)
- Max size: 10MB each

Output specifications:
- Format: PNG
- Resolution: Specified by size parameter or default 1280*1280
- Total pixels: 768*768 to 1280*1280
- Aspect ratio: 1:4 to 4:1

Prompt tips:
- Reference images as 'image 1', 'image 2', 'image 3' in your prompt
- Example: 'Generate using the style of image 1 and background of image 2'

uses nano-banana-pro internally: for each requested ``<width>x<height>``

target, regenerates the image with an adaptive prompt, and then

pixel-perfect.

x-fal-metadata.about:
FLUX Erase [pro] API — remove objects from images using a mask.

The mask is a black/white image where white (255) pixels mark the
region to erase and black (0) pixels mark the region to keep. The
mask must match the dimensions of the input image.

Safety: a fal-side ``@safety_checker_all`` decorator screens the
input image (the mask is excluded via ``ignore_fields`` because it
is a binary B/W shape, not real content). BFL's erase API also
performs its own server-side content moderation and surfaces
"Content Moderated" / "Request Moderated" polling statuses, which
``submit_and_poll`` translates into the standard NSFW response.
The BFL erase API does not accept a ``safety_tolerance``
parameter, so the BFL-side moderation uses its server default.

All usages of this model must comply with [FLUX.1 PRO Terms of Service](https://blackforestlabs.ai/terms-of-service/).

cns_power_gamma.title: CNS Power Gamma
cns_power_gamma.description: Exponent on the residual (1 - gamma). Higher concentrates noise more aggressively on unresolved bands; lower is gentler and flatter. No effect under 'approximation', where gamma is uniform.

cns_gamma_divider.title: CNS Gamma Divider
cns_gamma_divider.description: Divides gamma first, weakening the coloring (pushing it toward uniform white noise). Paper uses 1.73 for distilled/unguided and 25.0 for CFG/base, so raise this for the /base (CFG) endpoints.

cns_s_churn.title: CNS Noise Strength
cns_s_churn.description: How much stochastic (colored) noise is injected after each step. 0 = CNS off, i.e. pure deterministic flow-matching (identical to normal klein); higher = more stochasticity. Turn this first; the other CNS parameters only matter when s_churn > 0.

cns_alpha_tilt_end.title: CNS Alpha Tilt End
cns_alpha_tilt_end.description: Frequency tilt at the end of sampling. Positive boosts high frequencies (fine texture/detail); negative boosts low frequencies (structure). The default favors low-frequency structure at the end.

enable_safety_checker.title: Enable Safety Checker
enable_safety_checker.description: If set to true, the safety checker will be enabled.

enable_cns.title: Enable CNS
enable_cns.description: Enable Colored Noise Sampling (CNS), a stochastic SDE sampler. Off by default; when enabled the cns_* parameters below take effect.

cns_gamma_source.title: CNS Gamma Source
cns_gamma_source.description: Where the per-frequency progress signal gamma(f, t) comes from. 'approximation' is self-contained but uniform across bands, so the frequency shaping comes entirely from the alpha-tilt parameters. 'matrix' uses the precomputed per-band gamma for true spectral-bias-aware coloring (more noise to genuinely under-resolved bands).

loras.title: Loras
loras.description: List of LoRA weights to apply (maximum 3).

cns_alpha_use_fnorm.title: CNS Frequency-Weighted Tilt
cns_alpha_use_fnorm.description: Use a smooth, frequency-position-weighted tilt (exp(alpha * f)) instead of a flat (1 + alpha) multiplier.

num_images.title: Number of Images
num_images.description: The number of images to generate.

cns_alpha_exp_sharpness.title: CNS Exponential Tilt Sharpness
cns_alpha_exp_sharpness.description: How sharp the exponential tilt-interpolation curve is. Only used when exponential interpolation is enabled.

cns_energy_scale.title: CNS Energy Scale
cns_energy_scale.description: Global multiplier on the injected colored noise after variance normalisation. <1 slightly damps the kick, >1 amplifies it (paper: 0.98 unguided, 0.998 guided).

cns_alpha_exp_interp.title: CNS Exponential Tilt Interpolation
cns_alpha_exp_interp.description: Use an exponential (vs linear) curve for the start-to-end tilt transition across sampling steps.

cns_num_freq_bins.title: CNS Frequency Bins
cns_num_freq_bins.description: How many radial frequency bands the spectrum is split into. More bands = finer-grained coloring.

cns_alpha_tilt_start.title: CNS Alpha Tilt Start
cns_alpha_tilt_start.description: Frequency tilt at the start of sampling, interpolated toward the end value over steps. Positive boosts high frequencies (fine texture/detail); negative boosts low frequencies (structure).

cns_power_gamma.title: CNS Power Gamma
cns_power_gamma.description: Exponent on the residual (1 - gamma). Higher concentrates noise more aggressively on unresolved bands; lower is gentler and flatter. No effect under 'approximation', where gamma is uniform.

cns_gamma_divider.title: CNS Gamma Divider
cns_gamma_divider.description: Divides gamma first, weakening the coloring (pushing it toward uniform white noise). Paper uses 1.73 for distilled/unguided and 25.0 for CFG/base, so raise this for the /base (CFG) endpoints.

cns_s_churn.title: CNS Noise Strength
cns_s_churn.description: How much stochastic (colored) noise is injected after each step. 0 = CNS off, i.e. pure deterministic flow-matching (identical to normal klein); higher = more stochasticity. Turn this first; the other CNS parameters only matter when s_churn > 0.

'approximation' is self-contained but uniform across bands, so the frequency shaping comes entirely from the alpha-tilt parameters. 'matrix' uses the precomputed per-band gamma for true spectral-bias-aware coloring (more noise to genuinely under-resolved bands).

- E-commerce image editing (remove background clutter)
- Photo retouching and restoration

Works with: Objects, people, text, logos, and other visual elements

cns_power_gamma.title: CNS Power Gamma
cns_power_gamma.description: Exponent on the residual (1 - gamma). Higher concentrates noise more aggressively on unresolved bands; lower is gentler and flatter. No effect under 'approximation', where gamma is uniform.

cns_gamma_divider.title: CNS Gamma Divider
cns_gamma_divider.description: Divides gamma first, weakening the coloring (pushing it toward uniform white noise). Paper uses 1.73 for distilled/unguided and 25.0 for CFG/base, so raise this for the /base (CFG) endpoints.

cns_s_churn.title: CNS Noise Strength
cns_s_churn.description: How much stochastic (colored) noise is injected after each step. 0 = CNS off, i.e. pure deterministic flow-matching (identical to normal klein); higher = more stochasticity. Turn this first; the other CNS parameters only matter when s_churn > 0.

image_urls.description: The URLs of the images for editing. A maximum of 4 images are allowed.

cns_alpha_tilt_end.title: CNS Alpha Tilt End
cns_alpha_tilt_end.description: Frequency tilt at the end of sampling. Positive boosts high frequencies (fine texture/detail); negative boosts low frequencies (structure). The default favors low-frequency structure at the end.

enable_safety_checker.title: Enable Safety Checker
enable_safety_checker.description: If set to true, the safety checker will be enabled.

enable_cns.title: Enable CNS
enable_cns.description: Enable Colored Noise Sampling (CNS), a stochastic SDE sampler. Off by default; when enabled the cns_* parameters below take effect.

cns_gamma_source.title: CNS Gamma Source
cns_gamma_source.description: Where the per-frequency progress signal gamma(f, t) comes from. 'approximation' is self-contained but uniform across bands, so the frequency shaping comes entirely from the alpha-tilt parameters. 'matrix' uses the precomputed per-band gamma for true spectral-bias-aware coloring (more noise to genuinely under-resolved bands).

loras.title: Loras
loras.description: List of LoRA weights to apply (maximum 3).

cns_alpha_use_fnorm.title: CNS Frequency-Weighted Tilt
cns_alpha_use_fnorm.description: Use a smooth, frequency-position-weighted tilt (exp(alpha * f)) instead of a flat (1 + alpha) multiplier.

image_size.title: Image Size
image_size.description: The size of the generated image. If not provided, uses the input image size.

num_images.title: Number of Images
num_images.description: The number of images to generate.

cns_alpha_exp_sharpness.title: CNS Exponential Tilt Sharpness
cns_alpha_exp_sharpness.description: How sharp the exponential tilt-interpolation curve is. Only used when exponential interpolation is enabled.

cns_energy_scale.title: CNS Energy Scale
cns_energy_scale.description: Global multiplier on the injected colored noise after variance normalisation. <1 slightly damps the kick, >1 amplifies it (paper: 0.98 unguided, 0.998 guided).

cns_alpha_exp_interp.title: CNS Exponential Tilt Interpolation
cns_alpha_exp_interp.description: Use an exponential (vs linear) curve for the start-to-end tilt transition across sampling steps.

cns_num_freq_bins.title: CNS Frequency Bins
cns_num_freq_bins.description: How many radial frequency bands the spectrum is split into. More bands = finer-grained coloring.

cns_alpha_tilt_start.title: CNS Alpha Tilt Start
cns_alpha_tilt_start.description: Frequency tilt at the start of sampling, interpolated toward the end value over steps. Positive boosts high frequencies (fine texture/detail); negative boosts low frequencies (structure).

x-fal-metadata.about:
Qwen-Image-Edit-F2P - Generate full portrait from cropped face image

This endpoint takes a cropped facial image and generates a complete portrait including:
- Full body or upper body composition
- Clothing, pose, and setting as specified in the prompt
- Natural integration of the face into the generated portrait
- Consistent lighting and style throughout

Perfect for:
- Creating full portraits from ID photos or headshots
- Generating diverse portrait variations from a single face
- Character design and concept art
- Profile picture enhancement

Input: Cropped face image (closeup of face)
Output: Full portrait with specified clothing, setting, and style

Based on: https://huggingface.co/DiffSynth-Studio/Qwen-Image-Edit-F2P

Qwen-Image-Edit-Remover-General-LoRA - Remove unwanted elements from images

This endpoint cleanly removes specified elements (objects, people, text, etc.) from images while:
- Maintaining the consistency and quality of the rest of the image
- Automatically filling in the removed areas naturally
- Preserving the original image style and composition

Perfect for:
- Removing unwanted objects or people from photos
- Cleaning up product images (remove text, logos, watermarks)
- E-commerce image editing (remove background clutter)
- Photo retouching and restoration

Works with: Objects, people, text, logos, and other visual elements
The model maintains high fidelity of the remaining image content.

Based on: https://huggingface.co/starsfriday/Qwen-Image-Edit-Remover-General-LoRA

This endpoint takes a cropped facial image and generates a complete portrait including:
- Full body or upper body composition
- Clothing, pose, and setting as specified in the prompt
- Natural integration of the face into the generated portrait
- Consistent lighting and style throughout

Perfect for:
- Creating full portraits from ID photos or headshots
- Generating diverse portrait variations from a single face
- Character design and concept art
- Profile picture enhancement

Input: Cropped face image (closeup of face)
Output: Full portrait with specified clothing, setting, and style

Based on: https://huggingface.co/DiffSynth-Studio/Qwen-Image-Edit-F2P

x-fal-metadata.about:
Next Scene Qwen-Image-LoRA V2 - Create cinematic shot progressions and scene transitions

This endpoint generates natural cinematic transitions from one frame to the next, including:
- Camera movements (dolly shots, push-ins, pull-backs, tracking moves)
- Framing evolution (wide to close-up, angle shifts, reframing)
- Environmental reveals (new characters, expanded scenery, spatial progression)
- Atmospheric shifts (lighting changes, weather evolution, time transitions)

Perfect for:
- Storyboard generation for film and animation
- Cinematic AI video pipelines with frame coherence
- Sequential narrative workflows
- Concept art showing scene progression

Best results: Start prompts with "Next Scene:" and describe camera/scene changes

x-fal-metadata.about:
Next Scene Qwen-Image-LoRA V2 - Create cinematic shot progressions and scene transitions

This endpoint generates natural cinematic transitions from one frame to the next, including:
- Camera movements (dolly shots, push-ins, pull-backs, tracking moves)
- Framing evolution (wide to close-up, angle shifts, reframing)
- Environmental reveals (new characters, expanded scenery, spatial progression)
- Atmospheric shifts (lighting changes, weather evolution, time transitions)

Perfect for:
- Storyboard generation for film and animation
- Cinematic AI video pipelines with frame coherence
- Sequential narrative workflows
- Concept art showing scene progression

Best results: Start prompts with "Next Scene:" and describe camera/scene changes
Recommended LoRA strength: 0.7-0.8

Based on: https://huggingface.co/lovis93/next-scene-qwen-image-lora-2509

x-fal-metadata.about:
Qwen-Image-Edit-2509-Light-Restoration - Remove existing lighting and apply soft even light

This endpoint removes existing lighting and shadows from images and applies soft, even lighting:
- Removes harsh shadows, highlights, and directional lighting
- Applies neutral, soft illumination across the image
- Useful for creating clean lighting datasets
- Prepares images for relighting with other LoRAs

Perfect for:
- Creating training datasets for lighting LoRAs
- Normalizing lighting across photo collections
- Removing unwanted lighting effects
- Preparing images for consistent relighting

Note: This uses a fixed prompt optimized for lighting removal
Works best with: Portrait and product photography

Based on: https://huggingface.co/dx8152/Qwen-Image-Edit-2509-Light_restoration

x-fal-metadata.about:
Qwen Image Edit 2509 - Shirt Design LoRA - Put designs on people's shirts

This endpoint applies designs/graphics from your input image onto people's shirts:
- Takes a design/graphic from the first image
- Applies it naturally onto the shirt in the second image
- Maintains proper perspective and lighting
- Works with various shirt types and poses

Perfect for:
- Custom t-shirt design mockups
- Product visualization for apparel
- Virtual try-on for graphic tees
- Fashion design prototyping

Input: Provide 2 images - [design/graphic, person wearing shirt]
Trigger phrase: "put this design on their shirt"

Based on: https://huggingface.co/ostris/qwen_image_edit_2509_shirt_design

x-fal-metadata.about:
Qwen-Image-Edit-2509-Light-Restoration - Restore natural lighting with soft, even illumination

This endpoint restores natural lighting by removing harsh shadows and light spots:
- Removes harsh shadows, highlights, and directional lighting
- Removes visible light spots and shadows
- Applies neutral, soft illumination across the image
- Relights the image with soft, even light

Perfect for:
- Restoring photos with harsh or uneven lighting
- Normalizing lighting across photo collections
- Removing unwanted lighting effects
- Preparing images for consistent relighting

Note: This uses a fixed prompt optimized for lighting restoration - no prompt input needed
Works best with: Portrait and product photography

Based on: https://huggingface.co/dx8152/Qwen-Image-Edit-2509-Light_restoration
